info.title: CityTurfer API
info.description:
The CityTurfer HTTP API: the app's use cases over HTTP, to back up and sync a local-first phone and, later, other clients.

## Getting started

- **Base URL:** pick a server above. Locally, `pnpm --filter @cityturfer/api dev` runs the API on port 8787 and `pnpm run web:dev` serves this page at https://cityturfer.local/swagger with the API under `/api`.
- **Status:** sign-in, backup and restore are live: health, auth, `/v1/me`, consents, activity upload/read/rename/delete, track, gap routes, the changes feed, the Home City, the data export (e-mailed link), account settings (name, e-mail, optional password), account deletion, activity totals and server turf (summary, every cell, the claim of an activity: recomputed from uploaded tracks). Every route is live today; a route added ahead of its build is **planned**: its summary starts with `[planned]`, it carries `x-cityturfer-status: planned` and answers `501` once auth and validation pass. Live data routes answer `503 storage.unavailable` when the server has no database.
- **Auth:** `POST /v1/auth/codes` with an e-mail, then `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` with the 6-digit code from the e-mail: the answer's `token` goes in `Authorization: Bearer <token>` (button **Authorize**) for about 60 days (sliding); `DELETE /v1/auth/session` signs out. An account with a password may sign in with `{ email, password }` instead of the code. **The website** signs in (code or password) with `client: "browser"` and gets an `HttpOnly` cookie (`__Host-ct_session`, `Path=/`) instead of a token: 14 days sliding, at most 30 (8 hours with `sharedComputer`); its writes need `Origin` = the website and `CityTurfer-Client: web/<version>` (else `403 auth.csrf`). `GET /v1/auth/sessions` lists the signed-in phones and browsers. Device tokens (`API_TOKENS`) keep working for one more release. A missing token answers `401` *before* the input is validated. Locally the dev server prints the code (and with `AUTH_FIXED_CODE=000000`, addresses `@e2e.cityturfer.test` sign in with `000000`); `dev-token` works for user `admin` on PGlite.
- **Account settings:** `PATCH /v1/me` changes the name. A new e-mail or setting, changing or removing the password first needs a step-up code: `POST /v1/me/step-up/codes` mails one to the current address, the change spends it. Afterwards every other session (phones and browsers) is signed out; the one making the change stays. Device tokens get `403 identity.account-required`.
- **Consent:** activity and Home City writes need `PUT /v1/me/consents/cloud-sync` with `granted: true` first (else `403 consent.required`); Apple Health activities also `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`.
- **Headers you send:** `Content-Type: application/json`; `Content-Encoding: gzip` for long tracks; `If-Match` to change an existing activity; `CityTurfer-Client: ios/0.8.0+123` (old clients may get `426 client.too-old`; the website sends `web/<version>`).
- **Headers you get:** `X-Request-Id` on every answer, `Cache-Control: private, no-store` (unless a route says otherwise) and `Vary: Cookie, Authorization` on every `/v1` answer (quote it when reporting a problem), `ETag` on activities, tracks and `/v1/turf/cells` (send it back as `If-None-Match`: `304` when unchanged), `Location` on 201/202, `Retry-After` and `RateLimit` on 429.
- **Turf on the web:** download every cell with `GET /v1/turf/cells` (pages of up to 50,000 `[h3Id, walk, run, cycle]`, follow `nextCursor`; `410 turf.changed` mid-way → start again), keep its `ETag` and revalidate with `If-None-Match`. No bounding box or coordinates in any URL.
- **Limits:** request and response bodies ≤ 4.5 MB (Vercel); ≤ 40,000 points per track; gzip bodies inflate to ≤ 16 MB.

## Sync flow (phone ↔ server)

The phone is local-first and authoritative for what it recorded; the server stores activities with their tracks and recomputes everything derived (summaries, turf). Writes are keyed by ids the phone mints, so every request can be retried.

**First upload of an existing history**
1. `PUT /v1/me/consents/cloud-sync` (and `apple-health-in-cloud-sync` to include Apple Health imports).
2. `GET /v1/sync/changes` without a cursor, every page: what the server already has (the manifest).
3. For each local activity, oldest first (never `demo-…`): absent → `PUT /v1/activities/{id}`; same `trackHash` → done; different → `PUT` with `If-Match`; tombstoned → delete it locally.
4. `PUT /v1/activities/{id}/gap-routes` once the phone checked the gaps (an empty list when there are none); `PUT /v1/turf/home-city`.
5. Keep the last `nextCursor`.

**Restore to a new phone**
1. Sign in; `GET /v1/sync/changes` without a cursor while `hasMore` (entries carry ids, names, versions and `trackHash`, no geometry; a page ends at `limit` or about 1 MB).
2. Per activity: `GET /v1/activities/{id}` (summary, gap routes, `gapsCheckedAt`) and `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track`. Store them as restored: never upload them back.
3. Apply tombstones and the Home City; keep the last `nextCursor`.

**Every day after**
- **Push** from the outbox: recorded → `PUT`; track corrected → `PUT` + `If-Match`; renamed → `PATCH`; deleted → `DELETE`; gaps estimated → `PUT …/gap-routes`; Home City → `PUT /v1/turf/home-city`.
- **Pull** on launch and foreground: `GET /v1/sync/changes?cursor=…` while `hasMore`; fetch `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track` (with `If-None-Match`) only when `trackHash` is new; apply tombstones by deleting locally. Pull **before** importing from Apple Health, so a workout recorded on another phone is not imported twice.

**Conflicts:** same content → `200` (replay). Stale `If-Match` → `412`: pull, re-apply, retry. Different content without `If-Match` → `428`. Deleted id → `410 activity.deleted`: delete wins. Renames and the Home City: last write wins. Invalid cursor → `410 sync.cursor-expired`: start again without one.

## Errors

Every error is `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `code`. `detail` is for people and never repeats input values; a `400` lists JSON pointers in `errors[]`.

| code | status | meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `invalid-request` | 400 | Invalid request |
| `auth.missing` | 401 | Missing bearer token or session cookie |
| `auth.invalid` | 401 | Invalid or expired token |
| `auth.invalid-code` | 401 | Wrong or expired code: ask for a new one |
| `auth.invalid-credentials` | 401 | Wrong e-mail or password |
| `auth.csrf` | 403 | Cross-site request refused: send it from the CityTurfer website |
| `consent.required` | 403 | Give the cloud-sync consent first |
| `identity.account-required` | 403 | Sign in with your account (not a device token) to do this |
| `not-found` | 404 | Not found |
| `activity.deleted` | 410 | Activity was deleted |
| `sync.cursor-expired` | 410 | Sync cursor expired: sync again without a cursor |
| `turf.changed` | 410 | Your turf changed while you paged it: download it again from the first page |
| `export.gone` | 410 | This download link was used or has expired |
| `email.taken` | 409 | This address belongs to another account |
| `precondition-failed` | 412 | The resource changed since your version |
| `payload-too-large` | 413 | Request body too large |
| `unsupported-media-type` | 415 | Unsupported content type or encoding |
| `activity.track-too-short` | 422 | A track needs at least two points |
| `activity.ends-before-start` | 422 | The activity ends before it starts |
| `activity.invalid-name` | 422 | Names are 1 to 80 characters |
| `activity.track-hash-mismatch` | 422 | trackHash does not match the track |
| `activity.renamed-in-future` | 422 | renamedAt is more than 5 minutes ahead of the server |
| `activity.source-mismatch` | 422 | source does not match the id (hk-… is apple-health) |
| `home-city.unknown` | 422 | Not a catalogue city |
| `export.no-email` | 422 | The account has no e-mail to send the export link to |
| `display-name.too-long` | 422 | Names are at most 40 characters |
| `display-name.invalid` | 422 | Names cannot hold control characters |
| `email.invalid` | 422 | Not a valid e-mail address |
| `email.unchanged` | 422 | This is already the account address |
| `password.too-short` | 422 | Passwords are at least 12 characters |
| `password.too-long` | 422 | Passwords are at most 128 characters |
| `password.breached` | 422 | This password appears in known data breaches: choose another |
| `client.too-old` | 426 | Update the app to sync |
| `precondition-required` | 428 | Send If-Match to change an existing resource |
| `rate-limited` | 429 | Too many requests |
| `auth.rate-limited` | 429 | Too many codes or sign-ins: wait and try again |
| `internal` | 500 | Something went wrong |
| `not-implemented` | 501 | Not implemented yet |
| `storage.unavailable` | 503 | Storage is not available: retry later |

## Units and formats

JSON in camelCase. SI units with a suffix (`distanceM`, `movingS`, `areaKm2`). Timestamps ISO 8601 UTC; an activity may carry its IANA `timeZone` for display — the server derives nothing from local time. Coordinates `[lon, lat]` (GeoJSON order); bounding boxes `[west, south, east, north]`. Track points `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM]`. `trackHash` = SHA-256 hex of `JSON.stringify(track.points)` (no whitespace, ECMAScript number formatting, upload order); the server computes it, so sending it is optional. Turf cells are H3 indexes (resolution 11).

## Privacy

GPS tracks, turf cells and the Home City are personal data. Cloud sync needs the `cloud-sync` consent; everything can be exported (`POST /v1/me/exports`) and erased (`DELETE /v1/me`). Nothing of it is logged: logs hold the route pattern, status, duration, request id and user id. Examples on this page use public landmarks (Warsaw Old Town).

tags.name: Identity
tags.description: Sign-in with an e-mailed one-time code (Better Auth behind our own routes), sign-out and the signed-in user.

tags.name: Privacy
tags.description: Consents for cloud sync, the GDPR export (async, a file) and erasure of everything the server holds.

tags.name: Sync
tags.description: The one feed every device pulls: activity upserts, tombstones and the Home City since a cursor. Uploads go to the Activity Log. See **Sync flow** below.

tags.name: Activity Log
tags.description: Finished activities with their tracks, under ids the phone minted. Versioned (`ETag`, `If-Match`); deletes leave tombstones (`410` on re-upload).

tags.name: Territory
tags.description: Turf recomputed on the server from uploaded tracks (never uploaded by phones) and the Home City. Numbers can differ slightly from the phone's (upload order, float maths); the server's are canonical for server views.

bearerAuth.description: A session token from `POST /v1/auth/sign-in` (e-mailed code, about 60 days, sliding), or — for one more release — a device token minted with `pnpm --filter @cityturfer/api run token:new -- <userId>` (the server knows only its SHA-256, env `API_TOKENS`). Sent with `Authorization`, it wins over the cookie.

cookieAuth.name: __Host-ct_session
cookieAuth.description: The website's session (`POST /v1/auth/sign-in` with `client: "browser"`): `HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict; Path=/`, host-only, set on the website's host through its `/api/v1/*` rewrite. 14 days sliding, at most 30 days; on a shared computer a browser-session cookie and 8 hours. Requests that change something also need `Origin` = the website, `Sec-Fetch-Site: same-origin` when sent, and `CityTurfer-Client: web/<version>` (else `403 auth.csrf`).

ETag.description: Version of the resource; send it back in `If-Match` to change it.

Location.description: Where the created resource or job lives.

RateLimit.description: Remaining quota of the current window (IETF RateLimit header).

coreVersion.description: Version of `@cityturfer/core` the server computes summaries with.

database.description: Whether the database answers a trivial query (no details). Live data routes answer 503 unless `ok`.

CodeRequested.description: Empty: the same answer whether or not the e-mail has an account.

detail.description: For people; never holds input values or coordinates.

errors.description: Only on 400 `invalid-request`: which fields are invalid (the first 20).

ProblemCode.description: Stable machine code (catalogue in the API description, "Errors").

code.description: Why it is invalid (zod issue code).

token.description: Phones only — absent for `client: "browser"` (the cookie carries it and page scripts never see it). Bearer token: send `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Store it in the keychain; never log it.

expiresAt.description: Phones: about 60 days ahead, moved 60 days on when used after a day (sliding). Browsers: 14 days ahead, sliding the same way, never past `absoluteExpiresAt`.

absoluteExpiresAt.description: Browsers: the session ends then however often it is used (30 days, or 8 hours on a shared computer). Null for phones.

SessionClient.description: `phone`: the app, with a bearer token. `browser`: the website, with the session cookie.

SignInBody.description: Either the e-mailed code or the account password, for a phone or a browser session.

code.description: The 6-digit code from the e-mail (works once, 10 minutes).

allOf.description: Default `phone`: the token comes in the body. `browser`: the session goes in the `__Host-ct_session` cookie and the body has no token; the request must come from the website (`Origin`, `CityTurfer-Client: web/<version>`, else `403 auth.csrf`).

sharedComputer.description: Browsers only ("This is a shared computer"): the cookie lasts until the browser closes and the session at most 8 hours. `true` with a phone is `400`.

password.description: The account password (sign-in only: accounts are created by a code).
password.example: tram stops past the old town

allOf.description: Default `phone`: the token comes in the body. `browser`: the session goes in the `__Host-ct_session` cookie and the body has no token; the request must come from the website (`Origin`, `CityTurfer-Client: web/<version>`, else `403 auth.csrf`).

sharedComputer.description: Browsers only ("This is a shared computer"): the cookie lasts until the browser closes and the session at most 8 hours. `true` with a phone is `400`.

SessionList.description: Live sessions, most recently used first. Device tokens are not listed.

lastActiveAt.description: Last use, to the day: a session records its use at most once a day (also once its expiry can no longer move). A shared-computer session (8 hours) shows when it signed in.

expiresAt.description: When it signs out by itself unless used again.

SignedInDevice.description: One signed-in phone or browser. No IP address, user agent or location is stored.

name.description: The name the Turfer chose (at most 40 characters); null when none: show "You", never the id.

displayName.description: Deprecated since 0.5.0 (old phone builds): `name`, falling back to the user id. Read `name`.

hasPassword.description: Whether the account can also sign in with a password.

passwordChangedAt.description: When the password was set or last changed.

createdAt.description: When the server first saw the account.

name.description: Trimmed, at most 40 characters, no control characters; blank clears it.

code.description: The code mailed to the new address.

newPassword.description: 12 to 128 characters, any characters, spaces count; not in a known data breach.
newPassword.example: tram stops past the old town

status.description: `pending`: being built; `ready`: the link was e-mailed; `downloaded`: fetched at least once (still works until `expiresAt`); `expired`: 24 h passed, or a consent was withdrawn; `failed`: nothing was sent, ask again at once.

expiresAt.description: The e-mailed link works until then (24 h).

DataExportJob.description: An export of everything the server holds for the account: a zip with `data.json` (account, consents, activities with tracks and gap routes, tombstones, Home City) and one GPX 1.1 file per activity. The download link is only in the e-mail and works until `expiresAt`.

policyVersion.description: Privacy policy version shown to the user.

ConsentPurpose.description: `cloud-sync`: back up and sync activities with their GPS tracks. `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`: include workouts imported from Apple Health (decision D2). Without `cloud-sync` the server accepts no uploads.

nextCursor.description: Always present: store it and pass it next time, even when `hasMore` is false.

hasMore.description: True: ask again now with `nextCursor`. A page ends at `limit` changes or about 1 MB.

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

ActivityUpserted.description: Created or changed (track, name, gap routes). Download the track only when `activity.trackHash` differs from yours.

version.description: Grows by one with every change; the `ETag` is `"v<version>"`.

trackHash.description: Canonical track hash: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of `JSON.stringify(track.points)` — no whitespace, points `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM | null]` in upload order, numbers in ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (what `JSON.stringify` writes). The server computes it; a hash the client sends must match (422 `activity.track-hash-mismatch`). Tells other devices whether to download the track again.

ActivityFeedEntry.description: An activity in the changes feed: no preview or numbers (pages stay small). Fetch `GET /v1/activities/{id}` and, when `trackHash` is new, `GET /v1/activities/{id}/track`.

ActivitySource.description: `recording`: a finished Recording Session; `apple-health`: imported from Apple Health (`hk-…` id, needs the `apple-health-in-cloud-sync` consent); `import`: any other import. Demo history (`demo-…`) is never uploaded.

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

ActivityTombstone.description: Deleted: delete it locally and never upload it again (it would answer 410).

changedAt.description: When the server recorded the change.

HomeCityChanged.description: Apply when `chosenAt` is newer than yours (last write wins).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null at the end.

timeZone.description: IANA zone the phone reported; display only.

estimatedDistanceM.description: Part of distanceM estimated along streets over GPS gaps (D3).

trackHash.description: Canonical track hash: SHA-256 (lowercase hex) of the UTF-8 bytes of `JSON.stringify(track.points)` — no whitespace, points `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM | null]` in upload order, numbers in ECMAScript shortest round-trip form (what `JSON.stringify` writes). The server computes it; a hash the client sends must match (422 `activity.track-hash-mismatch`). Tells other devices whether to download the track again.

version.description: Grows by one with every change; the `ETag` is `"v<version>"`.

coreVersion.description: Version of the shared core that computed the numbers.

ActivityTotals.description: Every activity on the server, as the phone's Stats tab counts them: distance and moving time include the street estimates across GPS gaps.

timeZone.description: IANA zone; for activities recorded before sync, the phone sends its current zone.

resumedSegments.description: Segments that began with a manual Resume (tells a pause from a GPS gap); null when unknown.

trackHash.description: Optional (0.3.0): when sent, the server checks it against the canonical hash of `track.points`.

Track.description: Every point of an activity, in time order. Personal data.

TrackPoint.description: Columns: `[lon, lat, t, segment, altitudeM]` — longitude and latitude (degrees, WGS 84), time (epoch ms, UTC), segment number (a new segment starts after a pause or GPS gap; segments are never bridged), altitude in metres or null. Accuracy and speed are not sent (data minimisation, decision D1).

resumedSegments.description: Segments that began with a manual Resume; null when unknown.

renamedAt.description: When a `PATCH` last renamed it (the phone’s time); null when never renamed.

gapsCheckedAt.description: When the phone last checked the GPS gaps (`PUT …/gap-routes`, an empty list included); null when never checked or since the track changed. A restoring phone that sees a time here does not estimate the gaps again.

movingS.description: Moving time of this kilometre (not cumulative).

GapRoute.description: A street route the phone estimated across a GPS gap: counted in distance, drawn dashed, never claimed as turf. The server never computes these (D3).

name.description: The new name (1–80 characters once trimmed).

renamedAt.description: When the user renamed it on the phone: the latest `renamedAt` wins (offline-safe).

checkedAt.description: When the phone checked the gaps (`gapsCheckedAt`).

GapRoutesUpload.description: Replaces every gap route of the activity; an empty list means checked, no gaps.

turfVersion.description: The version of the turf this page belongs to (+1 on every change).

nextCursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last page.

TurfCellCounts.description: One Turf Cell: `[h3Id, walk, run, cycle]` — the H3 index (resolution 11) and how many activities of each type covered it. Visits = walk + run + cycle; strength (`1 − exp(−visits/3)`) and tier derive from visits with the Territory rules of the shared core, as on the phone. No polygon or centroid: draw the cell from its id (h3-js `cellToBoundary`).

Claim.description: The cells one activity covered. A cell is *new* for the claim with the earliest `(startedAt, activityId)` that covers it (decision D4), so the answer does not depend on upload order; it can change when an older activity arrives later.

cityId.description: A catalogue city id, or null to clear.

chosenAt.description: When the user chose it on the phone; the latest `chosenAt` wins (offline-safe).

get.description: Public. Answers `200` when the function is up; `database` tells whether the database answers a trivial query (it reads no user data and reveals no details).

post.description: Sends a 6-digit one-time code (valid 10 minutes) to the address (use case RequestSignInCode). Always `202 {}`, also for an address without an account: the account is created by the first successful sign-in. Limits: 1 code per address per minute, 3 per 10 minutes and 10 per day, 30 per IP (an IPv6 /64 counts as one IP) per 10 minutes (`429 auth.rate-limited` with `Retry-After`). While a code is still valid and not burnt, a new request mails the same code again (and extends it by 10 minutes) instead of replacing it.

202.description: Code sent if the address can receive it.

value.title: Invalid request

429.description: Too many codes or sign-ins: wait `Retry-After` seconds. Codes: `auth.rate-limited`.

value.title: Too many codes or sign-ins: wait and try again

503.description: No database configured or reachable: retry later. Codes: `storage.unavailable`.

value.title: Storage is not available: retry later

post.summary: Sign in with the code or the password
post.description: Exchanges the e-mailed code, or the account password, for a session (use cases SignIn and SignInWithPassword; Better Auth). A code creates the account on the first sign-in; a password never does. **Phones** (default, `client: "phone"`): a bearer `token` in the body, about 60 days, sliding. **Browsers** (`client: "browser"`, with a code or a password): no token in the body; the answer sets `__Host-ct_session=…; Max-Age=2592000; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict` (host-only; without `Max-Age` when `sharedComputer`), 14 days sliding, at most 30 days (8 hours on a shared computer); the request must come from the website (`Origin`, `Sec-Fetch-Site`, `CityTurfer-Client: web/<version>`, else `403 auth.csrf`). A wrong or expired code is `401 auth.invalid-code`; three wrong tries burn the code (ask for a new one). A wrong password, an account without a password and an unknown address are all `401 auth.invalid-credentials`. Limits (codes and passwords together): 10 sign-ins per address and 20 failed sign-ins per IP (an IPv6 /64 counts as one IP) per 10 minutes, and 10 failed sign-ins per address per day (then even the right code or password answers `429` until the day is over).

200.description: Signed in. Browsers: the session cookie is in `Set-Cookie`, the body has no token.

Set-Cookie.description: Browsers only: the session cookie (`HttpOnly`, so page scripts never read it).

delete.description: `scope=others` signs out every session of this account but the current one; `scope=all` every session, this one and every phone included (use case RevokeSessions). Phones then answer `401` on their next request and must sign in again; their recorded data stays on them. With the cookie, `all` also clears it. Device tokens are not sessions and keep working. Idempotent.

put.summary: Upload or replace a finished activity
put.description:
Stores the activity with its track under the id the phone minted (use cases ImportActivity and, for a corrected track, CorrectTrack). The server recomputes distance, time and splits from the track with the shared core and computes the canonical `trackHash` (a hash the client sends must match). Needs the `cloud-sync` consent (Apple Health activities also `apple-health-in-cloud-sync`).

- **New id** → `201` with `ETag` and `Location`.
- **Same content again** (same track, name and fields) → `200`, unchanged: replays are safe.
- **Different content** → send `If-Match` with the current `ETag`: `200` and version + 1; a stale one → `412`, none → `428` (both carry the current `ETag`). A new track drops the stored gap routes: send them again.
- **Deleted id** → `410 activity.deleted`: delete the activity locally too.

`source` must match the id: `hk-…` ids are `apple-health` and only they may be (else `422 activity.source-mismatch`).

Bodies are limited to 4.5 MB: send long tracks with `Content-Encoding: gzip`.

get.description:
Every Turf Cell of the user with its visits per type, sorted by cell id, a page at a time (use case ListTurfCells): the web map downloads the whole turf once and draws it locally. No bounding box and no coordinates in the URL — only an opaque cursor.

- **Pages:** follow `nextCursor` until null. The cursor is bound to `turfVersion`: if the turf changes meanwhile (an upload, a delete), the next page answers `410 turf.changed` — start again without a cursor.
- **Caching:** `ETag` names the turf version; send it as `If-None-Match` to get `304` (no body) when nothing changed. `Cache-Control: private, no-cache`.
